title: Hardware heterogeneity compatibility gate and testing harness for private runtime upgrades
content:
Summary:
This is a draft playbook for introducing a compatibility gate and lightweight test harness to validate runtime upgrades across heterogeneous private deployments (mixed GPU types, CPU-only nodes, and differing quantization capabilities). The goal: avoid large-scale failures when we deploy the new runtime/kernel combo and TF module changes to on-prem/VPC customers with mixed hardware.

Context / motivation:
- We see increasing variance in customer fleets: A100 + T4 + older V100s, and some bare-metal x86 nodes used as fallback.
- New runtime versions include kernel optimizations and quantization-friendly code paths that can behave differently across hardware and driver versions.
- Existing runbooks are focused on control-plane compatibility and API shims but do not provide a rapid validation loop for hardware heterogeneity.
- Past incidents: RED-3410 (cache corruption on mixed-NCCL clusters), RED-3921 (fallback path latency blowup).

Scope:
- Target scope: private deployments (VPC and on-prem) where operator has admin access to deploy a validation harness. Not intended for hosted customers.
- Validate: model-serving path (loading, KV cache, attention kernel selection), quantization toggles, TF module breaking changes (networking and IAM shims).
- Excludes: full data migration playbooks, billing/accounting changes.

Assumptions / prerequisites:
- Operator can create temporary namespaces or appliance slices in the customer cluster (or coordinate with their infra owner).
- Customer agreed to maintenance window or pre-prod mirror where applicable.
- Access to the test model artifacts (small deterministic model + sample prompts).
- TF modules in this release include a compatibility flag: enable_hardware_gate=true (we will add module notes below).

High-level approach:
1) Lightweight harness: small container set that exercises critical code paths with low request volume (smoke + stress).
2) Compatibility gate: a pass/fail criteria set that must be satisfied on a representative subset of nodes before full rollout.
3) Progressive rollout: node-level canary > slice canary > cluster-wide rollout with auto-fallback to previous runtime variant.
4) Observability + rapid rollback plan: explicit signal thresholds and a single-button revert in the orchestrator.

Compatibility gate details (pass/fail signals):
- Model load success rate: 100% load of test model on each hardware class within 30s.
- KV cache sanity: no KV cache mismatch or corruption on 100 iterative generate requests (deterministic checksums).
- Latency regression: median token latency per hardware class must be within 2x baseline and p95 within 3x.
- Memory safety: no OOM or kernel driver errors in dmesg within test window.
- Quantization correctness: output token sequences must match baseline within a small edit-distance threshold for deterministic prompts.

Test harness components (implementation notes):
- tester-runner image: runs deterministic generation suites against a local endpoint, emits JSON result blobs.
- hw-class-discovery script: queries node labels/annotations to map GPUs to hardware class (uses nvidia-smi / rocm-smi when available).
- small-models bundle: tiny LLM (~100M params distilled) compiled for multiple quantization levels for cross-checks.
- TF shim toggles: terraform variable to set a compatibility-only flag that wires in a test sidecar and grants minimal IAM for test traffic.

Terraform module notes (minimal changes required):
- new variable: enable_hardware_gate (bool, default false) -> when true, creates a test-namespace, service-account, and test runner daemonset.
- new outputs: hardware_gate_result_bucket (GCS/S3) and hardware_gate_status (string).
- guardrails: module will not promote control-plane change unless hardware_gate_status == "pass". This is implemented as a terraform null_resource local-exec that polls the test results endpoint (operator can opt out).
- migration advice: add the variable in customer modules and set enable_hardware_gate = true during controlled upgrades; support default=false for customers who decline.

Validation plan (step-by-step for on-prem operator):
- PREP: snapshot current runtime image tag and TF module commit. Ensure backup for KV and stateful services.
- STEP 0: Set enable_hardware_gate = true in TF staging workspace. Apply to create test namespace + daemonset.
- STEP 1: Start test-runner against representative nodes (label selection: use node selector with same labels as serving pool). Run smoke suite (model load + 20 generations).
- STEP 2: Run extended suite per hardware class: 1000 short requests distributed across classes, kv-checks and deterministic quant checks.
- STEP 3: Evaluate gate per pass/fail signals. Upload JSON results to hardware_gate_result_bucket.
- STEP 4A (PASS): proceed with node-level canary: update runtime image on 5% of nodes (low-traffic), monitor signals for 2 hours.
- STEP 4B (FAIL): capture logs, collect kernel traces, mark nodes for rollback and escalate to engineering.
- STEP 5: If node-canary good, expand to 20% slice canary, then 50%, then cluster-wide. At each step, re-run harness on newly updated nodes.

Rollback knobs / emergency actions:
- TF-level quick revert: re-apply previous runtime image tag using terraform workspace rollback helper.
- Orchestrator quick-switch: orchestrator has "fallback-variant" route to previous runtime compiled for older kernels.
- Cache invalidation: if KV checksum mismatches appear, isolate the node, flush locally cached KV prefix, rehydrate from primary store.
- Network-level mitigation: move traffic through edge proxy shim that forces a compatible code path (slower but safe).

Observability and telemetry needed:
- Test harness emits per-hardware-class JSON: success_rate, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, kv_checksum_hash, quant_edit_distance, errors[].
- Dashboard: Hardware Gate dashboard that groups by node label (gpu.type, driver.version) and shows gate_status.
- Alerts: threshold alerts for gate failure, driver panic logs, and memory OOM spikes.

Operational considerations / playbook tips (notes to self):
- Keep deterministic model small; operators dislike large downloads. Host artifacts on a CDN or prefetch in TF module.
- Be explicit about driver versions that are unsupported; consider a pre-upgrade driver check step.
- For customers with strict change windows, provide an "opt-in preflight" run that does not create daemonsets but validates node profiles offline.
- When quantization changes are involved, run an A/B eval on a subset of prompts to surface semantic drift early.

Unresolved questions / action items:
- (A) How do we handle appliances that cannot run the test runner due to network policy? -> fallback: operator-run binary with local artifact upload.
- (B) Should gate enforcement be mandatory for critical customers? ask legal/CS for SLAs.
- (C) Add an integration test in CI that simulates mixed hardware using emulation containers? Priya to prototype.

Post-mortem template (if gate fails in prod):
- Timeline of events, nodes affected by hardware class, which signal failed first, immediate mitigations taken, root cause hypothesis, long-term fix, owner, and target date.

Appendix: quick commands and snippets (work-in-progress)
- discover hardware class (example):
  kubectl exec -it tester-pod -- /usr/local/bin/hw-class-discovery --out /tmp/hw.json
- run harness locally:
  docker run --rm -e ENDPOINT=https://local-host:8080 tester-runner:canary --suite extended --result /tmp/result.json
- terraform snippet (module usage):
  module "runtime" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//runtime?ref=vX.Y.Z"
    enable_hardware_gate = true
  }

Notes: this is purposefully a lightweight draft to get feedback from field engineers and SREs. The next version should include an exact data schema for the JSON results, sample test vectors, and a concise one-click rollback CLI snippet.

Owners / next steps:
- Aisha R. (author) -> iterate on TF module impl with Miguel.
- Miguel O. -> prototype tester-runner and hardware discovery.
- Priya S. -> design dashboard and alerting.
- Jonah L. -> review rollbacks and orchestrator quick-switch logic.

Related tickets and references:
- RED-3410, RED-3921, RED-4872 (compatibility hub), GH PR: runtime#2143

End of draft.
